hints: Notice that yellow precipitate with alkaline iodine is the classic iodoform test, so focus on what structure in Y causes it.
Y must contain a methyl carbonyl group, $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$, which means it is either ethanal or a methyl ketone.
Work backwards from Y to X by asking which type of alcohol oxidises to give a methyl ketone.
walkthrough:
**Decode the test on Y**

Think of the yellow precipitate as a big clue. Alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ only with $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ and methyl ketones.

Test rule:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{C=O group} + \text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 \text{(yellow ppt)}$$

**Link Y back to oxidation of X**

Remember how alcohols oxidise. Primary gives aldehyde then acid, secondary gives ketone, tertiary is not oxidised.

$$\text{primary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid}$$
$$\text{secondary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ketone}$$

**Find which X gives a positive Y**

Since Y must be a methyl ketone (it comes from an alcohol, not from ethanal in this list), X must be the secondary alcohol that oxidises to $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Check the conclusion**

That secondary alcohol is butan-2-ol, and its ketone product contains $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ so it gives the yellow precipitate. This fits both statements perfectly.

options.A: Butan-1-ol is a primary alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. It oxidises to butanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, which does not contain the $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ group and so gives no yellow precipitate.
options.B: Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It oxidises to butan-2-one, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, a methyl ketone which gives a positive iodoform test with yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate.
options.C: Methylpropan-1-ol, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$, is a primary alcohol. It oxidises to 2-methylpropanal, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCHO}$, which is not ethanal and not a methyl ketone, so no yellow precipitate forms.
options.D: Methylpropan-2-ol, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$, is a tertiary alcohol. It has no hydrogen on the carbon bearing the OH group, so it resists oxidation and cannot form Y at all.
